subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In the systems approach to designing, what are the three main parts of a system?
questions.explain: The systems approach models every system as an input, a process and an output stage.

questions.q: What is the main role of an input device in a system?
options: It detects or senses a signal and sends it to the process
It produces movement, light or sound
It makes decisions about what the system should do
It supplies electrical power to the whole circuit
questions.explain: Input devices sense a change or signal and pass it on to the process block.

questions.q: On a systems block diagram, what do the arrows between blocks represent?
options: The direction in which signals or information flow
The physical size of each component
The amount of electrical power supplied
The order in which parts are assembled
questions.explain: Arrows show the flow of signals or information from one block to the next.

questions.q: Which of the following is an output device?
questions.explain: A buzzer produces an action (sound), so it is an output device.

questions.q: Which of the following is an input device?
questions.explain: A push switch senses a user action and provides a signal to the system, so it is an input.

questions.q: What best describes a closed-loop (feedback) system?
options: A system that uses feedback from its output to adjust its input
A system that has no output device
A system that can only be switched on and off manually
A system that runs for a fixed time and then stops
questions.explain: A closed-loop system feeds information about the output back to control the input.

questions.q: A security light must switch on only when it is dark AND movement is detected. Which pair of input sensors is needed?
options: A light-dependent resistor and a PIR sensor
A thermistor and a moisture sensor
questions.explain: An LDR senses darkness and a PIR sensor detects movement, providing both required inputs.

questions.q: Which component is a programmable device that can be given a set of instructions to control a system?
questions.explain: A microcontroller is a programmable component that stores and runs a program to control a system.

questions.q: What is a key advantage of using a microcontroller instead of many separate electronic components?
options: A single reprogrammable chip can replace many separate components
It removes the need for any input or output devices
It never needs an electrical power supply
It cannot be changed once the product is made
questions.explain: One reprogrammable microcontroller can carry out tasks that would otherwise need many components, saving space and allowing changes.

questions.q: How is a microcontroller most commonly programmed at GCSE level?
options: By producing a flowchart in programming software
By soldering extra resistors onto the chip
By changing the voltage of the battery
questions.explain: Flowchart-based software is used to write the sequence of instructions and download it to the microcontroller.

questions.q: In a flowchart used to program a microcontroller, which symbol is used to ask a yes/no question?
questions.explain: A diamond (decision) symbol represents a yes/no question that branches the program.

questions.q: A product must count how many times a button is pressed and switch on a lamp after 10 presses. Which part of the system carries out the counting and decision?
questions.explain: The process block, the microcontroller, counts the signals and decides when to switch on the output.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation LDR stand for?
questions.explain: An LDR is a light-dependent resistor whose resistance changes with light level.

questions.q: What happens to the resistance of an LDR as the light falling on it increases?
options: Its resistance stays exactly the same
questions.explain: In brighter light an LDR's resistance falls, which is how it senses light levels.

questions.q: Which physical change does a thermistor detect?
questions.explain: A thermistor is a temperature-sensing component whose resistance varies with heat.

questions.q: For a typical (NTC) thermistor, what happens to its resistance as the temperature rises?
questions.explain: A negative temperature coefficient (NTC) thermistor's resistance falls as it gets hotter.

questions.q: Which sensor is used to detect movement by sensing body heat?
questions.explain: A PIR sensor detects movement by sensing changes in infrared (heat) radiation.

questions.q: Why is a resistor usually connected in series with an LED?
options: To limit the current and prevent the LED being damaged
To make the LED brighter than its rating
To store energy for when the power is off
To change the colour of the LED
questions.explain: A series resistor limits the current through the LED so it is not damaged.

questions.q: A greenhouse fan must switch on automatically when the air becomes too hot. Which input sensor should be used?
questions.explain: A thermistor senses temperature, so it can trigger the fan when the greenhouse gets too hot.

questions.q: What does a moisture sensor detect in a system?
options: The presence of water or moisture
questions.explain: A moisture sensor responds to water or dampness, for example in a soil or rain-detecting system.

specSource: AQA GCSE Design and Technology (8552) specification; Systems Approach to Designing
